worklog.title: Work log
worklog.description: Catalogues that turn the billing rules into configuration: when work happened and what it costs relative to business hours, and where the logged time goes.

hour_types.title: Hour types
hour_types.description: When the work happened, and the multiplier that applies to it. One hour outside business hours costs the client more than one hour inside them.
hour_types.multiplier_hint: Applied to the logged hours to produce the equivalent hours. Values below 1 are allowed, for instance travel time at half rate.
hour_types.multiplier_invalid: Enter a number with up to two decimal places
hour_types.multiplier_too_small: Multiplier must be at least 0.01. Use a non-billable billing type to avoid charging.
hour_types.edit_warning: Changing the multiplier only affects work logged from now on. Entries already recorded keep the multiplier they were recorded with.

empty.title: No hour types yet
empty.description: Create an hour type so work logs can be classified and priced.

billing_types.title: Billing types
billing_types.description: Where the logged time goes: a contracted hour pool, an invoice, or nowhere. This is what a technician picks when the work falls outside the usual route.
billing_types.edit_warning: Changing the billing route only affects work logged from now on. Consider creating a new billing type instead, so past and future entries stay easy to tell apart in reports.

empty.title: No billing types yet
empty.description: Create a billing type so work logs know where the time goes.

billing_routes.debit_pool_hint: Draws from the client's contracted hours

holidays.title: Holidays
holidays.description: The days the classification engine treats as holidays. A holiday applies for the whole day and, by default, outranks the window of the weekday it falls on.
holidays.name: Name
holidays.is_recurring_hint_on: Applies on this day and month in every year, past and future. Use it for fixed dates like Christmas.
holidays.is_recurring_hint_off: Applies only to this exact date. Use it for dates that move, like Carnival, and enter each year separately.
holidays.scope_hint: Recorded for reporting. It does not filter anything yet.

empty.title: No holidays yet
empty.description: Add the holidays your contracts recognise, so work logged on them is classified automatically.

delete.title: Delete holiday
delete.description: {name} will stop being treated as a holiday. Work logs already recorded keep the hour type they were recorded with.
delete.description_recurring: {name} repeats every year, so deleting it removes the holiday from every future year as well. Work logs already recorded keep the hour type they were recorded with.

errors.covered_by_recurring: A yearly holiday already covers this day and reach. Edit that entry instead of adding a second one.
errors.collides_with_specific: A holiday already exists on this day and reach in another year. Remove it before making this one yearly.

created.title: Holiday added
created.message: Work logged on this day will be classified as a holiday.

not_created.title: Holiday not added
not_created.message: Something went wrong. Please try again.

updated.title: Holiday updated
updated.message: Work logs already recorded are unaffected.

not_updated.title: Holiday not updated
not_updated.message: Something went wrong. Please try again.

removed.title: Holiday deleted
removed.message: Work logs already recorded are unaffected.

not_removed.title: Holiday not deleted
not_removed.message: Something went wrong. Please try again.

errors.row: This row is missing a required value, or its recurrence is unreadable.
errors.date: This date could not be read.
errors.scope: This reach is not one of national, state or municipal.
errors.has_invalid_rows: Some rows could not be read.
errors.no_rows: There are no rows to import.

windows.title: Classification windows
windows.description: Which stretch of which kind of day maps to which hour type. The engine resolves an instant by taking the matching window whose hour type has the lowest priority number.
windows.border_hint: Use 24:00 for the end of the day. An end at or before the start means the window runs into the next day.
windows.crosses_midnight_hint: This window crosses midnight, so it continues into the following day.
windows.whole_day_hint: This window covers the whole day.
windows.empty_day: No window covers this kind of day, so work logged in it will not be classified.

health.complete: Every minute of the week is classified
health.complete_description: {count} windows, with no gaps and no conflicts.
health.incomplete: Part of the week is not classified
health.incomplete_description: Work logged in an uncovered range comes back with no suggested hour type, and the technician has to choose one. Existing work logs are unaffected.
health.overlaps: Windows the engine cannot decide between

delete.title: Delete classification window
delete.description: {range} will stop being classified as {hourType}. Work logs already recorded keep the hour type they were recorded with.

errors.overlap: Another window covers part of this range with the same priority, so the engine could not decide between them. Change one of the priorities or the ranges.
errors.would_break_coverage: This would leave part of the week unclassified. Cover the range with another window first.
errors.borders_must_differ: The borders must differ. Use 00:00 to 24:00 for a whole day.
errors.invalid_clock: Enter a time as HH:MM, for example 18:00 or 24:00.
errors.foreign_hour_type: That hour type belongs to another workspace.

service_prices.title: Hourly prices
service_prices.description: The base hour rate, by vigency. A readjustment adds a new vigency instead of editing the current one, so work already invoiced keeps the price it was billed at.
service_prices.empty: No price registered. Work logs for this client will be recorded without a value.
service_prices.first_of_month_hint: A vigency starts on the first of a month. That keeps a work log's price and a contract overage's price reading the same sheet.
service_prices.no_table: No price is in force on this date.
service_prices.override_hint: An absolute rate that replaces base x multiplier for this hour type. It already includes the multiplier.
service_prices.override_prompt: Absolute rate for this hour type (R$ per logged hour)

toasts.load_failed: The prices could not be loaded.
toasts.save_failed: The price could not be saved.
toasts.duplicate: A vigency already starts on that date.
toasts.not_first_of_month: A vigency has to start on the first of a month.
toasts.already_priced: This vigency already priced work logs and cannot be removed. Those records keep the rate they were billed at, and deleting it would leave nobody able to check it.

service_permissions.guest_hint: A client user cannot hold work log grants.
service_permissions.admin_hint: An Admin already holds all three; there is nothing to grant.

errors.guest: A client user cannot hold work log grants.
